description:
Add Playwright end-to-end tests that exercise the real running stack (docker compose: web + Postgres + token auth) from the outside, verifying PROMPT.md behavior works in the actual app rather than only in Django's test client. Requested directly by Forrest.

Context: unit/integration coverage already exists (12 APITestCase tests in app/telemetry/tests.py, run against Postgres). These e2e tests are the 'does the deployed stack actually work' layer: real HTTP against the compose web service, real token auth, real Postgres.

Decisions to be made in planning: Python playwright (pytest-playwright) vs Node — the repo is Python-only, so prefer Python unless a strong reason emerges; Playwright's APIRequestContext is the right tool since this is a JSON API with no browser UI (admin UI smoke test optional). Test setup must provision a user + token non-interactively (e.g. docker compose exec web manage.py shell -c ... or a management command) and must clean up or use unique devEUIs per run so tests are re-runnable against a persistent DB.

Scope: e2e test suite, any tiny helpers needed for non-interactive token provisioning, README section on running them, and whatever dependency/config files the chosen runner needs. Tests must cover at minimum: happy-path ingest of the PROMPT.md example (201, passing), duplicate fCnt → 409, failing value (AA==), unauthenticated → 401, and that Device.latest_status flips (observable via a second payload or the admin/DB).

Convention reminder: commit .lattice/ changes along with the work (see CLAUDE.md).
title: Add Playwright end-to-end tests against the running compose stack
